sources.snippet: 💡 Overview Masked diffusion language models (LLaDA, Dream, DiffuLLaMA, …) decode by filling a fixed-size canvas. Unlike an autoregressive decoder, which generates until it emits EOS, a masked diffusion decoder must be told how many target slots to fill before denoising begins.

sources.title: [2502.09992] Large Language Diffusion Models - arXiv.org
sources.snippet: The capabilities of large language models (LLMs) are widely regarded as relying on autoregressive models (ARMs). We challenge this notion by introducing LLaDA, a diffusion model trained from scratch under the pre-training and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) paradigm. sources.snippet: The training objective of LLaDA is an upper bound on the negative log-likelihood of the model distribution, making LLaDA a generative model. This enables LLaDA to naturally perform in-context learning, instruction-following, and ensures Fisher consistency for scalability with large datasets and models.
